title: Electronic Structure of Atoms (Electron Configurations)
lead: The electrons of an atom fill its orbitals in order of increasing energy, under the Aufbau principle, the Pauli exclusion principle and Hund’s rule. The electron configurations and orbital diagrams that result separate core from valence electrons and tie each element to its place in the periodic table, and they extend to ions.
objectives: Derive the predicted ground-state electron configurations of atoms
Identify and explain exceptions to predicted electron configurations for atoms and ions
Relate electron configurations to element classifications in the periodic table
summary_html:
The relative energy of the subshells determine the order in which atomic orbitals are filled (1s, 2s, 2p, 3s, 3p, 4s, 3d, 4p, and so on). Electron configurations and orbital diagrams can be determined by applying the Pauli exclusion principle (no two electrons can have the same set of four quantum numbers) and Hund’s rule (whenever possible, electrons retain unpaired spins in degenerate orbitals).

Electrons in the outermost orbitals, called valence electrons, are responsible for most of the chemical behavior of elements. In the periodic table, elements with analogous valence electron configurations usually occur within the same group. There are some exceptions to the predicted filling order, particularly when half-filled or completely filled orbitals can be formed. The periodic table can be divided into three categories based on the orbital in which the last electron to be added is placed: main group elements (s and p orbitals), transition elements (d orbitals), and inner transition elements (f orbitals).

exercises.prompt: Read the labels of several commercial products and identify monatomic ions of at least four transition elements contained in the products. Write the complete electron configurations of these cations.

answer.solution: A multivitamin and mineral tablet is one such product. Its label lists ferrous fumarate, zinc oxide, cupric sulfate and manganese sulfate, which contain the transition metal cations Fe2+, Zn2+, Cu2+ and Mn2+. Each configuration starts from the neutral atom, and because these are transition metals the 4s electrons are lost before any 3d electrons, as Example 6.11 shows for iron. Fe, 1s22s22p63s23p64s23d6, gives Fe2+: 1s22s22p63s23p63d6. Zn, 1s22s22p63s23p64s23d10, gives Zn2+: 1s22s22p63s23p63d10. Copper is one of the exceptions of Figure 6.29, with the configuration 1s22s22p63s23p64s13d10; it loses its 4s electron and one 3d electron, so Cu2+: 1s22s22p63s23p63d9. Mn, 1s22s22p63s23p64s23d5, gives Mn2+: 1s22s22p63s23p63d5. Each ion has as many electrons as the atomic number minus the charge: 24, 28, 27 and 23.

exercises.prompt: Read the labels of several commercial products and identify monatomic ions of at least six main group elements contained in the products. Write the complete electron configurations of these cations and anions.

answer.solution: For example, Na+: 1s22s22p6; Ca2+: 1s22s22p63s23p6; Sn2+: 1s22s22p63s23p63d104s24p64d105s2; F–: 1s22s22p6; O2–: 1s22s22p6; Cl–: 1s22s22p63s23p6.

exercises.prompt: Using complete subshell notation (not abbreviations, 1s22s22p6, and so forth), predict the electron configuration of each of the following atoms: (a) C (b) P (c) V (d) Sb (e) Sm

answer.solution: (a) C: 1s22s22p2; (b) P: 1s22s22p63s23p3; (c) V: 1s22s22p63s23p64s23d3; (d) Sb: 1s22s22p63s23p64s23d104p65s24d105p3; (e) Sm: 1s22s22p63s23p64s23d104p65s24d105p66s24f6. The number of electrons in each atom is its atomic number: 6, 15, 23, 51 and 62. The electrons fill the subshells in the order of Figure 6.26, 1s, 2s, 2p, 3s, 3p, 4s, 3d, 4p, 5s, 4d, 5p, 6s, 4f, each subshell taking its capacity (2 for s, 6 for p, 10 for d, 14 for f) before the next begins. Carbon ends with two electrons in 2p, phosphorus with three in 3p, vanadium with three in 3d after 4s is full, antimony with three in 5p, and samarium with six in 4f after 6s is full; in each case the superscripts add up to the atomic number.

exercises.prompt: Is 1s22s22p6 the symbol for a macroscopic property or a microscopic property of an element? Explain your answer.

answer.solution: It is the symbol for a microscopic property. The configuration 1s22s22p6 describes how the ten electrons of a single neon atom are arranged in its orbitals: two in the 1s orbital, two in the 2s orbital and six in the three 2p orbitals. A macroscopic property, such as density or boiling point, is observed or measured in a sample large enough to see and handle. The electron configuration belongs to each atom, which is far too small to see, so it belongs to the microscopic domain, even though it is inferred from macroscopic observations such as spectra and it accounts for macroscopic behavior such as the lack of reactivity of neon.

exercises.prompt: What additional information do we need to answer the question “Which ion has the electron configuration 1s22s22p63s23p6”?

answer.solution: The charge on the ion.

exercises.prompt: Draw the orbital diagram for the valence shell of each of the following atoms: (a) C (b) P (c) V (d) Sb (e) Ru

answer.solution: (a) C, valence shell 2s22p2: the 2s box holds a pair of arrows, one up and one down, and of the three 2p boxes two hold a single upward arrow and one is empty. (b) P, valence shell 3s23p3: the 3s box holds a pair of arrows, and each of the three 3p boxes holds a single upward arrow. (c) V, valence electrons 4s23d3: the 4s box holds a pair of arrows, and of the five 3d boxes three hold a single upward arrow and two are empty. (d) Sb, valence shell 5s25p3: the 5s box holds a pair of arrows, and each of the three 5p boxes holds a single upward arrow. (e) Ru, valence electrons 5s14d7, one of the exceptions of Figure 6.29: the 5s box holds a single upward arrow, and of the five 4d boxes two hold a pair of arrows and three hold a single upward arrow. In every diagram Hund’s rule places one electron in each orbital of a subshell, with parallel spins, before any orbital takes a second electron of opposite spin.

exercises.prompt: Using complete subshell notation (1s22s22p6, and so forth), predict the electron configurations of the following ions. (a) N3– (b) Ca2+ (c) S– (d) Cs2+ (e) Cr2+ (f) Gd3+

answer.solution: (a) N3–: 1s22s22p6; (b) Ca2+: 1s22s22p63s23p6; (c) S–: 1s22s22p63s23p5; (d) Cs2+: 1s22s22p63s23p64s23d104p65s24d105p5; (e) Cr2+: 1s22s22p63s23p63d4; (f) Gd3+: 1s22s22p63s23p64s23d104p65s24d105p64f7. An anion gains electrons in the Aufbau order: N, 1s22s22p3, takes three more 2p electrons, and S, 1s22s22p63s23p4, takes one more 3p electron. A main group cation loses the electrons added last: Ca loses its two 4s electrons, and Cs loses its single 6s electron and then one 5p electron, leaving 53. A transition or inner transition metal loses its highest s electrons first. Chromium is observed as 1s22s22p63s23p64s13d5 (Figure 6.29), so Cr2+ loses the 4s electron and one 3d electron, leaving 22. Gadolinium is observed as 1s22s22p63s23p64s23d104p65s24d105p66s24f75d1; Gd3+ loses the two 6s electrons and the 5d electron, leaving the half-filled 4f7 subshell and 61 electrons.

exercises.prompt: Which atom has the electron configuration 1s22s22p63s23p63d74s2?

answer.solution: It is cobalt, Co. The superscripts add up to 2 + 2 + 6 + 2 + 6 + 7 + 2 = 27, and a neutral atom has as many electrons as its atomic number, so the atomic number is 27. The configuration also places the element: after the argon core, 1s22s22p63s23p6, the 4s subshell is full and the 3d subshell holds seven electrons, which is the seventh element of the first transition series, in period 4 and group 9.

exercises.prompt: Which of the following atoms contains only three valence electrons: Li, B, N, F, Ne?

answer.solution: Boron contains only three valence electrons. The valence electrons of these main group atoms are the electrons in the shell of highest n. Li, 1s22s1, has one; B, 1s22s22p1, has three, the two 2s electrons and the one 2p electron; N, 1s22s22p3, has five; F, 1s22s22p5, has seven; and Ne, 1s22s22p6, has eight. The periodic table agrees, since boron is in group 13, whose atoms all have the valence configuration ns2np1.

exercises.prompt: Which atom would be expected to have a half-filled 6p subshell?

answer.solution: Bismuth, Bi, atomic number 83, has a half-filled 6p subshell. A p subshell holds six electrons in its three orbitals, so it is half-filled with three, one in each orbital by Hund’s rule. In the filling order, 6p follows 6s, 4f and 5d, so the element must have the xenon core plus 6s24f145d106p3, a total of 54 + 2 + 14 + 10 + 3 = 83 electrons. Its configuration is 1s22s22p63s23p64s23d104p65s24d105p66s24f145d106p3, and it is the period 6 member of group 15, whose atoms all end in np3.

exercises.prompt: In one area of Australia, the cattle did not thrive despite the presence of suitable forage. An investigation showed the cause to be the absence of sufficient cobalt in the soil. Cobalt forms cations in two oxidation states, Co<sup>2+</sup> and Co<sup>3+</sup>. Write the electron structure of the two cations.

answer.solution: Co2+: 1s22s22p63s23p63d7; Co3+: 1s22s22p63s23p63d6. The cobalt atom has 27 electrons, with the configuration 1s22s22p63s23p64s23d7. Cobalt is a transition metal, so its cations lose the 4s electrons before any 3d electrons, as Example 6.11 shows for Fe2+. Co2+ loses both 4s electrons and keeps 25 electrons, seven of them in 3d. Co3+ loses both 4s electrons and one 3d electron, keeping 24 electrons, six of them in 3d.

exercises.prompt: Thallium was used as a poison in the Agatha Christie mystery story “The Pale Horse.” Thallium has two possible cationic forms, +1 and +3. The +1 compounds are the more stable. Write the electron structure of the +1 cation of thallium.

answer.solution: 1s22s22p63s23p64s23d104p65s24d105p66s24f145d10

exercises.prompt: Write the electron configurations for the following atoms or ions: (a) B<sup>3+</sup> (b) O<sup>–</sup> (c) Cl<sup>3+</sup> (d) Ca<sup>2+</sup> (e) Ti

answer.solution: (a) B3+: 1s2; (b) O–: 1s22s22p5; (c) Cl3+: 1s22s22p63s23p2; (d) Ca2+: 1s22s22p63s23p6; (e) Ti: 1s22s22p63s23p64s23d2. An ion has the atomic number minus the charge in electrons. B, 1s22s22p1, loses its 2p and both 2s electrons, leaving 2. O, 1s22s22p4, gains one 2p electron, giving 9. Cl, 1s22s22p63s23p5, loses three of its 3p electrons, the last ones added, leaving 14. Ca, 1s22s22p63s23p64s2, loses its two 4s electrons, leaving 18. Titanium is a neutral atom with 22 electrons; after the 4s subshell is full, the last two enter 3d.

exercises.prompt: Cobalt–60 and iodine–131 are radioactive isotopes commonly used in nuclear medicine. How many protons, neutrons, and electrons are in atoms of these isotopes? Write the complete electron configuration for each isotope.

answer.solution: Co has 27 protons, 27 electrons, and 33 neutrons: 1s22s22p63s23p64s23d7. I has 53 protons, 53 electrons, and 78 neutrons: 1s22s22p63s23p63d104s24p64d105s25p5.

exercises.prompt: Write a set of quantum numbers for each of the electrons with an n of 3 in a Sc atom.

answer.solution: Scandium, 1s22s22p63s23p64s23d1, has nine electrons with n = 3: two in 3s, six in 3p and one in 3d. Each set is written (n, l, ml, ms). The 3s electrons have l = 0 and ml = 0 and differ in spin: (3, 0, 0, $+\frac{1}{2}$) and (3, 0, 0, $-\frac{1}{2}$). The 3p electrons have l = 1, and each of the three ml values holds a pair of opposite spins: (3, 1, –1, $+\frac{1}{2}$), (3, 1, –1, $-\frac{1}{2}$), (3, 1, 0, $+\frac{1}{2}$), (3, 1, 0, $-\frac{1}{2}$), (3, 1, +1, $+\frac{1}{2}$), (3, 1, +1, $-\frac{1}{2}$). The single 3d electron has l = 2 and may take any ml from –2 to +2, since the five 3d orbitals are degenerate, and as an unpaired electron it takes ms = $+\frac{1}{2}$, for example (3, 2, –2, $+\frac{1}{2}$). No two of the nine sets are the same, as the Pauli exclusion principle requires.

exercises.prompt: Atoms of which group in the periodic table have a valence shell electron configuration of ns2np3?
Atoms of which group in the periodic table have a valence shell electron configuration of ns2?

answer.solution: The atoms of group 2, the alkaline earth metals beryllium, magnesium, calcium, strontium, barium and radium, have the valence shell configuration ns2. Elements in one group have the same number of valence electrons in the same kind of subshell. In group 2 the s subshell of the outer shell is filled with two electrons and nothing follows it: Be is [He]2s2, Mg [Ne]3s2 and Ca [Ar]4s2, and so on down the group. Helium, 1s2, has the same form with n = 1, but it is placed in group 18 because its filled shell makes it a noble gas like the other members of that group.

exercises.prompt: Explain why Al is a member of group 13 rather than group 3?

answer.solution: Aluminum belongs to group 13 because its last electron enters a p subshell, not a d subshell. Its configuration is 1s22s22p63s23p1, so its three valence electrons are 3s23p1, the same form, ns2np1, as boron above it, 2s22p1. The elements of group 3, such as scandium, 1s22s22p63s23p64s23d1, also have three valence electrons, but theirs are ns2(n – 1)d1, with the last electron in a d subshell. The periodic table groups elements by the subshell being filled and the number of electrons in it, and the first d subshell, 3d, is not filled until after 4s, so aluminum in period 3 has no d electrons and sits in the p block with boron, whose chemistry it resembles.
